sections.html:
Midvale sits in the middle of the Salt Lake Valley, with the Jordan River on its western edge and Interstate 15 running through the center. The 2020 count was 36,028 residents, up from 27,964 in 2010, a 28.8 percent jump driven partly by new housing on the old smelter ground on the west side.

The median value of an owner-occupied home is $436,600 and median gross rent is $1,597. Only 43.4% of households own their home, so a seller here is often a landlord, an heir to a rental, or an owner with a tenant still living in the house. That shapes almost everything below: leases, licenses and closing dates matter as much as the condition of the roof.

sections.h2: Bingham Junction and the old slag site
sections.html:
Bingham Junction is the redeveloped 446 acres on Midvale's west side where five smelters processed lead and copper ore from 1871 to 1958. The EPA lists it as the Midvale Slag Superfund site and issued a Ready for Reuse Determination in 2008, which cleared the ground for commercial and residential use. Today it has a light rail station that opened in 2011, several kinds of homes, offices, a supermarket and a park.

South of it, Jordan Bluffs covers 351 acres and was part of the same slag ground. Redevelopment there is at an early stage, with proposals that could bring around 3,500 homes.

  • If your house is on the west side, a buyer or their lender may ask about the site's history, so hold on to any closing or cleanup paperwork you received when you bought.
  • For a specific parcel, the title company can tell you what it found.
  • Newer townhomes and condos near the station come with many different loan types, which can affect how a buyer finances a nearby house.

sections.h2: Getting around: TRAX, I-15 and main roads
sections.html:
Midvale has two TRAX light rail lines, Interstate 15 and a short drive to Interstate 215, so most commutes in the valley are workable from here. Average travel time to work is 20.6 minutes. When you describe the house to a buyer, distance to a station is worth a line.

  • The Red Line stops at Bingham Junction and runs to the University of Utah.
  • The Blue Line stops at Midvale Fort Union and Midvale Center.
  • 7800 South crosses the middle of the city east to west, and Main Street (700 West) runs through the historic downtown.
  • The I-15 and I-215 interchange is near 7200 South and State Street, and a ski bus runs along 7200 South.

Retail concentrates at the Shops at Fort Union on the east side and along State Street. Canyons School District covers most Midvale addresses, though boundaries shift, so confirm a specific address with the district before you promise a school in a listing.

The ground is the larger physical risk in this valley. The Wasatch Fault runs along it, and the Salt Lake City segment last ruptured about 1,200 to 1,300 years ago. Experts give a 57 percent chance of a magnitude 6.0 or larger quake somewhere on the fault within 50 years. Many Wasatch Front areas sit on soft Lake Bonneville sediments, which raises liquefaction risk, and a magnitude 5.7 quake near Magna in March 2020 shook the whole valley.

On an older Midvale house, a buyer's inspector will usually look at chimneys, water heater strapping and foundation cracks. You can repair them, disclose them, or sell as-is and let the buyer deal with them. Each route has a cost, and weighing the three is part of deciding how to sell.

A landlord in Midvale needs a city landlord business license. These licenses expire August 31 and are due no later than September 15. Most other business licenses expire December 31 and are past due after January 15.

The city council sets fee amounts every year, and moving a business to a new address in the city triggers new inspections. If you are selling a rental, make sure your license is current before a buyer's agent asks. Have the lease, the rent roll and the license handy, since a buyer who keeps your tenants will want to see all three.

sections.h2: Property tax dates and the residential exemption
sections.html:
Salt Lake County values and bills Midvale property on one schedule for the whole county. Everything is valued as it stood on January 1.

StepWhen
Assessor certifies valuesMay 22
Valuation notices mailedJuly and August
Board of Equalization window45 days from the original mailing
Tax notices mailedBy November 1
Last day to pay without penaltyNovember 30
Taxes become delinquentDecember 1

A Utah home that is someone's primary residence is taxed on 55 percent of its market value, thanks to a 45 percent residential exemption. The exemption does not carry over automatically after a sale, so the new owner has to file. Applications go to the county Board of Equalization by September 15.

The county recorder at 2001 South State Street, Suite N1-600, takes deeds Monday through Friday from 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. The office does not prepare documents or notarize them, and it does not decide whether a title is clear. Originals come back by mail two to three weeks after they are processed and imaged. In a normal sale the title company files the deed for you, so you will rarely visit the counter yourself.

sections.h2: How a cash sale works for a Midvale seller
sections.html:
A cash sale follows the same recording path as any other sale, but it skips the buyer's loan, the appraisal and the repair negotiation. The steps are short.

  • You tell us about the house, including any tenants and what needs work.
  • We review it and make an offer based on its condition.
  • If the offer suits you, a title company handles the signing and the recording at the county.
  • The closing date is set with you and the title company.

Houses with tenants, deferred repairs or inherited paperwork can be sold as they stand. If the offer does not suit you, you can turn it down.

faqs.q: What is the population of Midvale, Utah?
faqs.a: Midvale had 36,028 residents in 2020, up 28.8 percent from 27,964 in 2010. The estimate shown at the top of this page is the more recent figure.

faqs.q: When are Midvale property taxes due?
faqs.a: November 30 is the last day to pay current-year real property tax without penalty. Taxes become delinquent on December 1.

faqs.q: Is Midvale in Canyons School District?
faqs.a: Yes, Canyons is the main district for Midvale, with four elementary schools, two middle schools and Hillcrest High School. Check the district's boundary lookup for a specific address.

faqs.q: Do I need a license to rent out a house in Midvale?
faqs.a: Yes, Midvale requires a landlord business license. Landlord licenses expire August 31 and are due no later than September 15.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Midvale house that has tenants in it?
faqs.a: Yes. Many Midvale sellers are landlords, since owner-occupancy is only 43.4 percent. Share the lease and rent roll with the buyer early so the closing date can account for the lease terms.
